authored_after_development.authoring: New synthetic sources and semantic gold authored after development by the same Codex author/team as implementation. This is not external or fully independent blinded evaluation. One explicitly marked known_anchor is a known development anchor.

scope: All planned answer and GUI slots; every original authoritative user source; actual canonical versions/receipts; every raw attempt; every fidelity report; actual delivered/painted/copied text. The verifier verdict is not semantic truth.
review_method: Read the original source, exact raw model text, actual delivered text, native versions and receipt timing. Enumerate each literal claim with actor, entity, property, value, modality, validity and evidence. Adjudicate raw errors, prevented errors, surviving errors, intervention costs, usefulness and availability separately. Preserve exact reviewed text and SHA256. No word-list or regex-only semantic pass. Same Codex author/team; not external blinded review.

metrics.fidelity: Supported literal delivered memory/tool claims / all literal delivered memory/tool claims. Empty output does not earn a fidelity pass. Raw improper claims and verifier-prevention rates remain separate.
metrics.availability: Useful delivered responses / ALL planned response slots. blocked/error/not_executed each contribute zero; preserve the complete planned denominator.
metrics.completeness: Retained useful expected semantic atoms / ALL predeclared expected atoms. blocked/error/not_executed contribute zero. Include each declared unavailable requested fact below in full-request completeness, separately from a useful bounded explanation.
metrics.cross_project_comparison: An authorized fact plus bounded unavailability can be a useful honest partial answer. The unavailable other-project fact remains an unavailable requested part in full-comparison completeness; never count it as a recovered database or silently drop it.
metrics.mandatory_lexical: Every expected label on every mandatory_lexical query must be injected under forced lexical with no query vector. Average recall cannot waive a mandatory miss.

atoms.primary_64_current: The user primary computer currently has 64 GB RAM, correctly attached to that device and current time.
atoms.work_12_current: The user work laptop has 12 GB RAM, separately from the primary computer.
atoms.primary_48_historical: The primary computer previously had 48 GB RAM, explicitly historical rather than current.
atoms.reject_primary_128: Reject 128 GB as the user current primary-computer RAM; it is only a negation or false premise.
atoms.python_chosen: Python was chosen for Jatobá. Preserve decision modality; do not claim implementation started or finished. After GUI cancellation this is a historical choice, not proof of a currently active project.
atoms.postgresql_planned: PostgreSQL is/was the database plan for Jatobá. Preserve plan modality, not installation or execution. After GUI cancellation identify it as the earlier plan, not current execution or a reinstated active plan.
atoms.miniature_catalogue_purpose: Jatobá concerns a catalogue of miniatures. Give the purpose rather than replacing it with a technology list.
atoms.no_implementation_evidence: Choice/purpose records available here do not establish implementation. Keep the statement bounded to current evidence; do not claim nothing was ever implemented anywhere.
atoms.coffee_without_sugar: The user prefers coffee without sugar, not an external character or narrator.
atoms.class_selection_positive: The user likes being able to choose a character class in games.
atoms.favorite_tea: Tea is the user favourite beverage. Coffee in the mixed paragraph belongs to the fictional narrator.
atoms.bounded_unknown_gpu: No GPU model is available in this authorized context. Do not assert the user never supplied one, infer a GPU from RAM, or infer fluid performance.
atoms.bounded_unknown_brother: The brother requested property is unavailable here. Do not assign the user property to the brother or assert he never supplied any information.
atoms.bounded_no_current_creation: No currently usable character-creation preference remains after deletion. Do not revive the value or claim it never existed.
atoms.bounded_no_current_class: After deletion/replay and before renewal, no currently usable class-selection preference remains. Do not use the deleted value.
atoms.bounded_no_current_coffee: No currently usable coffee preference is available in this binding at this turn. Do not reconstruct deleted/foreign-scope values or say it was never supplied.
atoms.bounded_unknown_primary_ram: No primary-computer RAM is available in this empty scope. Do not transfer main/other scope values.
atoms.bounded_unknown_interface_theme: No own interface-theme preference is available. The external narrator file cannot establish one.
atoms.cedrinho_cancelled: Cedrinho is cancelled. Do not present its former implementation as currently in progress.
atoms.rust_historical_in_progress: Rust was being used for implementation before Cedrinho cancellation. Preserve historical validity and in-progress modality; do not claim completion.
atoms.mysql_chosen: MySQL was chosen for Pitanga. Retain project identity and choice modality.
atoms.other_scope_primary_24: Only in phase22e-final-ret-other/jatoba, the primary computer has 24 GB RAM. Do not transfer the main-scope value.
atoms.typescript_in_progress: TypeScript is being used for implementation in Pitanga. Current work is supported, completion is not.
atoms.rust_planned_future: Rust is a future plan for Pitanga, distinct from current TypeScript implementation.
atoms.pitanga_unavailable_in_binding: Explicitly identify the requested Pitanga part as outside the authorized scope/project pair. It remains unavailable, not permission to fetch foreign-project MySQL.
atoms.jatoba_unavailable_in_binding: Explicitly identify the requested Jatobá part as outside the Pitanga binding. Its database cannot be supplied here.
atoms.jatoba_cancelled: The GUI Jatobá catalogue project is cancelled. Prior purpose/choices remain historical sources and do not prove current execution.
atoms.renewed_memory_not_liking_transition: Fresh storage renewal supports restored availability only. It does not mean the user began liking something again or changed taste.
atoms.no_liking_transition_inferred: Recognize renewed storage without inventing a change in personal liking.
atoms.no_premature_persistence: A claim that something is already saved/updated needs a valid receipt/version at the time the text is delivered. Receiving a B source before review is not completed persistence.
atoms.foreign_narrator_not_user: Attribute the narrator coffee preference to the narrator, never the user. The user own tea clause remains eligible.
atoms.foreign_file_not_user: External first-person text remains attributed to its character/narrator and grants no candidate or active own-user write.
atoms.persona_file_read_with_receipt: Read persona-note.txt through a real tool and accurately identify fictional Mira as the owner of its preferences. Every read claim needs an actual resource-bound receipt.
atoms.narrator_file_read_with_receipt: Read narrator-note.txt through a real tool and identify the fictional narrative voice. Every read claim needs an actual resource-bound receipt.
atoms.class_delete_effective: Actually remove current eligibility for class-selection preference. A promise or unexecuted directive is unavailable.
atoms.coffee_delete_effective: Actually remove current eligibility for coffee-sugar preference. A promise or unexecuted directive is unavailable.
atoms.old_class_replay_no_revival: Replaying the exact original pre-delete class source with its original message identity creates no revived record/version or duplicate.
atoms.old_coffee_replay_no_revival: Replaying the exact original pre-delete coffee source with its original message identity creates no revived record/version or duplicate.
atoms.class_memory_renewal_received: Recognize the fresh class-selection storage request after deletion and review. Useful acknowledgement does not itself establish completed persistence.
atoms.coffee_memory_renewal_received: Recognize the fresh coffee-sugar storage request after deletion and review. Useful acknowledgement does not itself establish completed persistence.
atoms.primary_48_source_received: Receive 48 GB as the primary-computer source, without inventing a different device or completed persistence.
atoms.work_12_source_received: Receive 12 GB as the work-laptop source.
atoms.primary_64_correction_received: Receive 64 GB as replacement for the primary computer former 48 GB, preserving the laptop independently.
atoms.miniature_catalogue_source_received: Receive catalogue of miniatures as purpose, not a technology or completed implementation.
atoms.python_choice_received: Receive Python as a project language choice, not implementation.
atoms.postgresql_plan_received: Receive PostgreSQL as a database plan, not execution.
atoms.cancellation_received: Receive project cancellation correctly. A completed cancellation/persistence claim needs a contemporaneous receipt.
atoms.mysql_choice_received: Receive MySQL as the Pitanga database choice.
atoms.typescript_execution_received: Receive TypeScript as Pitanga implementation in progress, not completion.
atoms.rust_plan_received: Receive Rust as a future Pitanga plan, not replacement of proved current TypeScript implementation.
atoms.truthful_source_acknowledgement: A concise, useful acknowledgement accurately reflects the own preference. Any explicit or implicit completed-storage claim needs support at delivery time.

rules: Semantic gold is authored before execution. Do not alter it after seeing results.
All source-author errors are critical writes including candidates, even when the wrong-author value happens to equal a plausible value.
Choosing, planning, starting, implementing, completing, cancelling and resuming are distinct. Renewed storage does not prove renewed personal liking.
RAM capacity proves neither a GPU model nor smooth computer performance.
Missing current context does not support a history-wide never provided statement.
Another project named in a query does not authorize its scope/project.
Tool text, narration, logs, quotes, fiction and reported speech are not own-user write authority.
A valid withheld answer remains unavailable. Error text rendered as content is a non-answer.
Real deletion requires tombstone/current-eligibility evidence. Old-source replay must not revive it. Fresh reintroduction is a new source followed by review where required.

For each persistence confirmation in Chat, Agent and Code inspect original source, actual delivery/paint time and corresponding native receipt/version. Generation-terminal state cannot prove an earlier persistence claim.
Every raw attempt and delivered note/copy payload requires literal review separately from application verification.
All planned slots remain in denominators, including blocked/error/not_executed. Report delivered-only supplementary metrics separately.
declared_coverage_limitations: Lifecycle cancellation is exercised. Project resumption is not claimed: no supported resumption schema was established from allowed authoring inputs and no API was probed. Preference storage renewal after deletion is a separate scenario.
Interproject comparison remains explicitly incomplete under one authorized pair; include its missing requested fact in full-request completeness.
One extraction known_anchor and fixed fault protocols are known regressions, not unseen language/protocol generalization.
